issue.title: chat_install still starts the AXE orchestrator directly after a chat-driven update, bypassing the service host
issue.description: Chat-driven updates restart the scheduler through start_axe_daemon instead of the service host's scheduler service proc. See the bug body for the location, reproduction, and fix.

task_type_fields.impact: A chat-driven update can start a second scheduler behind the service host's back: the host either races it for the orchestrator lifecycle lock or sees a scheduler it doesn't own. That is the double-supervisor race this epic existed to remove. Fix: route the post-update restart through `restart_after_update()` / `restart_service_proc("scheduler", actor=..., reason="chat update")` from `sase.service.actions` (as `sase update` / `sase flag` / `sase plugin` now do), retitle the messages to "scheduler", then delete `start_axe_daemon`, the `_restart_axe_impl` helper, and whatever of `start_axe_daemon_result` / `_process_start.py` loses its last caller (keep `canonical_axe_start_command`, which `service/executable.py` needs). Related, not a duplicate: sase-14x (39 duplicate `sase service run`/`scheduler run` copies on athena, root cause undiagnosed and predates this path's retarget).
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by sase-11y.10.1.3.1.5 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2), confirmed by the sase-11y.10.1.3.1 land agent on master b87c8e3ee.

After a chat-driven update, `_update_worker` in `src/sase/integrations/chat_install.py` calls `_ensure_axe_running()` (lines ~193 and ~203). When `is_axe_running()` is false it calls `_restart_axe()` -> `_restart_axe_impl(start=start_axe_daemon, ...)`, which spawns a detached orchestrator directly (`_build_axe_start_command` now execs `sase scheduler run`), outside the SASE service host.

Epic sase-11y.10.1.3.1 made the service host the only CLI path that starts, restarts, or stops the scheduler (ensure watchdog, systemd scope wrapper, update restart, and `sase axe` lifecycle verbs all retired). The service_host_sunset plan never listed this sixth path, so it survived: `start_axe_daemon` / `start_axe_daemon_result` are kept alive only for it. Its user-facing strings still say "axe restart failed" and `_chat_install_worker.py` logs "axe restart succeeded".

Reproduce by reading the code: `git grep -n "_ensure_axe_running\|start_axe_daemon" src/sase/integrations`.

payload.description: Also about duplicate scheduler instances on athena; different root cause (service run itself is duplicated), but a fix here removes one non-host path that can spawn a scheduler
The service-host sunset epic whose plan never listed this sixth direct-start path
